source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Two soil-associated pests are highlighted as damaging to banana's underground parts. White grub larvae (ដង្កូវ, the larval stage of a scarab-type beetle) feed on roots and the corm, weakening the plant and stunting growth; adult beetles are also shown as contributing to damage. Farmers are advised to keep the base of the plant clean of debris where beetles can lay eggs, and where infestation is heavy, a labeled insecticide such as Nemathorin 10G (foadhiazate) can be applied around the base at roughly 20 grams per plant.

A separate corm-feeding weevil bores into the corm and lower stem tissue, creating tunnels that weaken the plant's structural support and provide entry points for rot organisms; management again centers on field sanitation and, when needed, a registered insecticide applied according to label instructions.
